details: Ships first-party REST server (`server/adkrest/`) with `POST /run_sse` (SSE) for streaming and `GET /run_live` (WebSocket via gorilla/websocket) for bidirectional live, plus a one-shot `POST /run`. Also ships an A2A JSON-RPC server and Vertex Agent Engine emulator. Both SSE and WS are core, default routes.

`AgentOS` produces a FastAPI app exposing `POST /agents/{agent_id}/runs?stream=true` as SSE by default, with `get_websocket_router` for WebSocket transport. Background-run resumable SSE is supported. SSE is the canonical client transport.
Library-only, no bundled server. Separate `AutoAgents-CLI` repo wraps it but is out of scope. `run_stream` returns an in-process iterator; serialization to SSE/WS is host work.
SDK is library-only over a stdin/stdout CLI subprocess. No FastAPI/Starlette adapter shipped. Users wrap `query()`/`ClaudeSDKClient` in their own SSE endpoint.
Library-only. Browser sub-export accepts `websocket: { url }` but the WS server is the user's responsibility. The `bridge.mjs` path targets claude.ai's hosted endpoint, not a server you run yourself.
OSS framework ships no HTTP server. AMP (closed/managed) provides `POST /kickoff` with webhook-based event push (not SSE/WS chat). Self-hosters wrap `Crew(stream=True)` themselves.
No `net/http` serving in core eino; no shipped server. In-process runtime uses `*AsyncIterator[*AgentEvent]` channel; you write the SSE handler yourself.
`genkit.Handler` returns an `http.HandlerFunc` with SSE via `?stream=true` or `Accept: text/event-stream`. No WebSocket support, no HTTP/2 push. Each flow is mounted manually on your `http.ServeMux`.

`langgraph-api` (closed-source / source-available paid platform) exposes SSE over `POST /threads/{tid}/runs/stream` and `GET .../stream` for resume. OSS repo ships only the runtime, checkpointers, client SDK and CLI shell — not the server.
`llama-index-core` is library-only. Recommended path is FastAPI + SSE over `handler.stream_events()`. Companion `llama_deploy` is a separate project.

`@mastra/server` is a Hono-based HTTP server with `POST /agents/:id/stream` returning SSE (streamFormat: 'sse'). Library-shaped — pass Mastra instance to `createMastraServer` and routes auto-register. WebSocket reserved for OpenAI realtime voice.

Several optional servers: DevUI (FastAPI, OpenAI Responses-compatible, beta `sample app, not for production`), AG-UI (rc, SSE), A2A (beta), Foundry hosting, Azure Functions, ASP.NET Core building blocks. SSE is standard. No single canonical multi-tenant production HTTP surface yet.
Library only; `Runner.run_streamed` yields a Python async iterator. Realtime sibling speaks WebSocket to OpenAI's hosted realtime API, not to your clients. No stock SSE adapter.

No first-party HTTP server. The `@openai/agents-extensions/ai-sdk-ui` package adapts a `StreamedRunResult` to Vercel AI SDK's SSE format, so SSE is achievable as an extension wrapper. No bundled server framework.

Two first-party surfaces: `agent.to_web()` returns a Starlette app and `UIAdapter.dispatch_request` plugs into Starlette/FastAPI. Both stream SSE via `_event_stream.py`. `to_web()` is positioned for local dev; UIAdapter is the production composable.
Rig is library-only. `Stream<MultiTurnStreamItem<R>>` is in-process; SSE/WebSocket framing is the user's job. No SSE adapter shipped.
Default is library-only. Optional `A2AServer` (FastAPI) wraps an Agent as Google A2A endpoint for agent-to-agent comms, plus experimental bidi voice. No first-party REST/SSE chat server.

Library-only by default; optional `A2AExpressServer` exposes an `InvokableAgent` as A2A JSON-RPC at `POST /` with `GET /.well-known/agent-card.json`. Not a multi-tenant chat server. Transports per upstream `@a2a-js/sdk`.

`createAgentUIStreamResponse` / `pipeAgentUIStreamToResponse` return SSE-shaped `Response`/pipe a `ServerResponse`. `JsonToSseTransformStream` is the canonical wire format with `x-vercel-ai-ui-message-stream: v2` header. SSE only; user mounts in Next.js/Express/Hono.

Wire is `data: <json Event>\n\n` for every `models.Event`, covering user/model messages, function calls, function responses, partials, errors. Linked to `FunctionCall.ID` for tool tracking. No explicit start/end SSE frame types but the iterator's lifecycle is observable.

SSE frames carry typed events: `RunStarted`, `ToolCallStarted`, `ToolCallCompleted`, `RunCompleted` (with metrics), `RunPausedEvent`, etc. Each is `event: <name>\ndata: <json>` shaped. Tool calls keyed by `tool_call_id`.

Rich `Event` enum (`ToolCallRequested`, `ToolCallCompleted`, `StreamChunk::ToolUseInputDelta`, etc.) all `Serialize/Deserialize`, but only available in-process via `Environment::subscribe_events`. Host writes the wire format.
In-process `Message` dataclasses (Assistant/User/Tool/Stream/Task events) are rich and stable; partial messages available via `include_partial_messages=True`. Wire encoding to SSE is consumer-side.

Iterator yields fully typed `SDKMessage`s including `SDKAssistantMessage`, tool progress, partial messages, system init. Wire framing left to user; recommended pattern is one SDKMessage per SSE `data:` frame.

AMP webhook delivers batched typed events (151 `BaseEvent` subclasses including `llm_call_started`, `tool_usage_finished`). Doc explicitly notes order is not guaranteed and recommends `realtime=true` at cost. In-process `StreamChunk` available for self-hosted but no SSE framing shipped.
`*AsyncIterator[*AgentEvent]` provides rich typed events in-process; serialization is host code. No first-party wire format.

SSE frames are `{message: ModelResponseChunk}` per chunk and `{result: ModelResponse}` for terminal frame. Includes role-tool / role-model content with `ToolRequest.Ref`. No dedicated tool-input-start/delta sub-event taxonomy.

Multiple stream modes (`values`, `updates`, `messages`, `messages/partial`, `messages/complete`, `checkpoints`, `tasks`, `tasks/result`, `custom`, `debug`, `error`, `metadata`, `end`, `feedback`) selectable per call. Events keyed for resume by `last_event_id`.
`handler.stream_events()` yields typed Pydantic `Event` models including `AgentStream`, tool events, `InputRequiredEvent`. Wire framing to SSE is BYO.

Forwarded `fullStream` includes `start`, `tool-call-input-streaming-start`, `tool-call-delta`, `tool-call`, `tool-result`, `tool-output` (long-tool progress), `tool-call-approval`, sub-agent execution chunks, `finish` etc. All keyed by `toolCallId`.

DevUI wire format is OpenAI Responses-compatible (`response.created`, `response.output_item.added`, `response.completed`, function_call_arguments.delta, function_approval events). AG-UI uses typed AG-UI protocol events.
`stream_events()` yields `RawResponsesStreamEvent`, `RunItemStreamEvent`, `AgentUpdatedStreamEvent`, etc. — rich and typed but serialization to SSE is host code.
`StreamedRunResult` iterates `RunStreamEvent` including `raw_model_stream_event` deltas. `ai-sdk-ui` extension converts to Vercel UI Message stream. No built-in wire framing.

`UIAdapter` emits Vercel AI Data Stream or AG-UI typed events: `start`, `text-delta`, `tool-call`, `tool-result`, `finish` with usage. Underlying loop yields typed `PartDeltaEvent`/`ToolCallPartDelta`.
`MultiTurnStreamItem` and `StreamedAssistantContent` are `Serialize+Deserialize` (serde `tag=type`) so usable on the wire, but Rig itself ships no serializer/handler.
`agent.stream_async` yields typed events (`init_event_loop`, `tool_use_stream`, `message`, `result`, etc.) with `toolUseId` linkage. Wire framing is host code.

`agent.stream()` yields `BeforeInvocationEvent`, `ContentBlockEvent`, `ToolStreamUpdateEvent`, `AfterToolCallEvent`, `InterruptEvent`, `AgentResultEvent`. Each event class has `toJSON()` for wire serialization. SDK does not enforce a wire format.

Canonical wire format `x-vercel-ai-ui-message-stream: v2` with `start`, `start-step`, `text-delta`, `tool-input-start`, `tool-input-delta`, `tool-input-available`, `tool-output-available`, `tool-approval-request/response`, `finish-step`, `finish`, `[DONE]`. Client `useChat` consumes this natively.

Default OSS REST router registers no auth middleware (`handler.go:37-60`). An example `AuthInterceptor` exists for the A2A path but hardcodes the user. Tenant scoping flows through user-supplied `stateDelta` and `context.Context` middleware you wrap yourself.

Built-in JWT middleware (`libs/agno/agno/os/middleware/jwt.py`) fills `request.state.user_id/scopes/accessible_resource_ids`. Per-route `Depends(require_resource_access(...))` enforces RBAC; scope schema `agent-os:<os-id>:<resource-type>:<resource-id>:<scope>` plus admin wildcard. Shared-secret fallback via env.
No HTTP boundary to terminate auth at.
SDK has no HTTP awareness; auth termination is the host's responsibility.
No JWT/OAuth validation in SDK. The bridge path needs an Anthropic OAuth token to talk to claude.ai but that is for the SDK-to-claude.ai direction, not for terminating your end-user auth.
OSS: BYO entirely. AMP provides bearer-token-per-automation but no first-party JWT/RBAC at request boundary.
No HTTP layer means no auth boundary; you wire your own.

`firebase.AuthContextProvider` plugin terminates Firebase Auth. Custom `ContextProvider` lets you read bearer tokens, validate, and populate `ActionContext`. No general-purpose JWT validator shipped; everything else is BYO middleware in front of `genkit.Handler`.

`langgraph-api` invokes `@auth.authenticate` on every request and `@auth.on.*` per-resource handlers apply filters. Identity flows into `runtime.context` / `ctx.user.identity`. Fully terminates at the API boundary.
No HTTP layer; auth is the host's responsibility.

`coreAuthMiddleware` terminates auth at the `/api/*` boundary (JWT/cookies/API keys). Integrates first-party with auth0/clerk/workos/supabase/firebase/better-auth/okta/studio. Auto-derives RBAC permissions from path+method; FGA via WorkOS.

DevUI ships bearer-token auth on by default with `DEVUI_AUTH_TOKEN`; `--no-auth` only for loopback. AG-UI / A2A / Foundry / Functions rely on host framework middleware. No first-party JWT-validation/tenant-scoping in production-positioned surfaces.
No SDK-level auth surface; host middleware validates and feeds identity into `RunContextWrapper.context`.
No auth handling in SDK; host middleware does JWT/API-key validation before calling `run()`.
Docs explicitly say `Treat the adapter endpoint as an internal backend service, running it inside your own authenticated route handler`. The adapter intentionally is not an auth boundary.
No HTTP surface; auth is the host's middleware.
No first-party auth boundary; A2A and BYO HTTP both delegate to the host.
`A2AExpressServerConfig.userBuilder` integrates with `@a2a-js/sdk`'s `UserBuilder` for per-request user resolution on the A2A path only. BYO HTTP path delegates entirely.
SDK does not parse `Authorization` headers; host framework (Next.js middleware, Hono auth, etc.) terminates auth before calling `createAgentUIStreamResponse`.

`GET .../sessions/{session_id}` returns full event list for client replay. No dedicated `/resume` endpoint — resumption is implicit by reusing the same `sessionId` on `/run_sse`. Live (bidi) path uses Gemini's `SessionResumptionConfig`.

`POST /agents/{agent_id}/runs/{run_id}/resume` reconnects to in-flight `asyncio.Task` and replays buffered SSE then continues live. `GET .../runs/{run_id}` returns persisted run, and `GET .../sessions/{session_id}/runs` lists runs per session.
No HTTP surface; in-process there is no resume primitive either.
`ClaudeAgentOptions.resume=<session_id>` re-opens a session on disk (or via SessionStore). There is no resume endpoint — it is a parameter when spawning a new client.
`query({ options: { resume: sessionId } })` and `resumeSessionAt: messageUuid` are SDK options; you build the endpoint. SDK provides logic, not the route.
OSS: `Crew.from_checkpoint(config)` is the in-process resume API; you wire `POST /sessions/:id/resume` yourself. AMP: redeploy and re-kickoff; replay via Studio UI.
`Runner.Resume(ctx, checkPointID)` exists at the Go API level; HTTP exposure is your job.

`X-Genkit-Stream-Id` request header re-subscribes to a durable stream via `StreamManager` (in-memory or Firestore-backed). First call writes the stream id; subsequent calls replay from durable store. No general session-reopen endpoint.

`GET /threads/{tid}/runs/{rid}/stream?last_event_id=...` resumes the SSE stream from last delivered event id (when created with `stream_resumable: true`). Plus state endpoints `GET /threads/{tid}/state`, historical `state/{checkpoint_id}`, and HITL resume via `command: {resume: ...}`.
Pattern is to serialize `Context` to your store keyed by `session_id` and pass `ctx=` to `workflow.run(...)`. No endpoint shipped.

`GET /agents/:id/observe-stream` attaches mid-stream as observer (resumable, multi-client). `POST /agents/:id/resume-stream` resumes suspended runs (generic tool.suspend). `GET /agents/:id/subscribe-thread` SSE subscribes a thread's runs.

DevUI: resending same `conversation` id pulls thread history automatically. AG-UI propagates `availableInterrupts` and `resume` metadata via `AGUIChatClient`. No dedicated replay/re-attach to an in-flight stream.
`RunResult.to_state().to_json()` + `RunState.from_json(agent, json)` is the primitive. No endpoint shipped; host builds `POST /runs/{id}/resume`.
`RunState.toString()` + `RunState.fromString(agent, str)` round-trips state for HITL/resume; the endpoint and persistence are BYO (next.js example only).

No dedicated resume endpoint; clients send full `messages` history on every request (Vercel AI / AG-UI design). For server-authoritative history persist by `conversation_id` and pass `message_history` to the adapter.
With `ConversationMemory`, calling `agent.prompt(...).conversation(\user-123\")` again resumes. No HTTP endpoint shipped."
`session_manager=FileSessionManager(session_id=...)` restores prior messages. `Agent.take_snapshot` / `load_snapshot` are building blocks. No endpoint.

`SessionManager.restoreSnapshot({ target: agent })` hydrates an Agent from `snapshot_latest`. Resume an interrupted run via `agent.invoke([interruptResponseBlock])`. Replay of past events is not a primitive.

Recipe in `examples/next/app/api/chat/[id]/stream/route.ts` uses third-party `resumable-stream` + Redis with `createResumableStreamContext`. Re-attaches via `GET /api/chat/[id]/stream`. Not part of `ai` proper but documented and supported.

SSE handler reads `req.Context()` so the client closing the SSE connection cancels the context and propagates into `Runner.Run`. No explicit `DELETE /run/{id}` endpoint; no AbortSignal framing inside SSE.

`POST /agents/{agent_id}/runs/{run_id}/cancel?session_id=...` calls `agent.acancel_run` which sets a cancellation flag observed by `raise_if_cancelled` checkpoints inside the run loop (multiple safe points).
`Environment::shutdown` drains the whole runtime; per-task cancel is BYO via a `CancellationToken` you check in a hook. No HTTP cancel endpoint.

`ClaudeSDKClient.interrupt()` sends a `control_request: interrupt` to the CLI which handles mid-LLM-call / mid-tool-call cancellation. `stop_task(task_id)` cancels a specific sub-agent. No HTTP endpoint, but a stable primitive.

`Query.interrupt()` and `Query.close()` over the JSON control protocol (`SDKControlInterruptRequest`); also `Options.abortController.abort()`. HTTP cancel endpoint is BYO mapping `DELETE` to `q.interrupt()`.

OSS: no in-process cancel API at all. `Crew.kickoff()` runs to completion; the bus surfaces `SigTermEvent`/`SigIntEvent` but no `Crew.cancel()`. AMP has no documented mid-flight cancel endpoint either. Real gap for long-running agent runs.
No first-class cancel API; cancellation is via `context.CancelFunc` propagating through Go ctx. No abort-run endpoint shipped.

Standard HTTP request cancellation propagates via Go `context.Context` for non-durable runs. Durable streaming detaches with `context.WithoutCancel`, so closing the connection does NOT cancel the underlying flow. Dev UI reflection API has cancel for traced actions but is dev-mode.

`POST /threads/{tid}/runs/{rid}/cancel?action=interrupt|rollback&wait=0|1` halts and persists an interrupt marker or rolls back state. `on_disconnect: cancel` option auto-cancels on SSE disconnect at creation time.
`WorkflowHandler.cancel_run()` is the in-process API; HTTP endpoint exposure is BYO.

`AbortSignal` is wired from HTTP layer into `agent.stream(..., { abortSignal })`; dropping the connection cancels. No explicit `DELETE /runs/:id`. `POST /agents/:id/signals` can carry an application-defined stop signal if the agent's signal schema includes one.
DevUI exposes `POST /v1/responses/{response_id}/cancel`. Also auto-cancels on client disconnect. AG-UI / A2A / Foundry rely on host conventions.
`RunResultStreaming._cancel_mode` (`none`|`immediate`|`after_turn`) and `result.cancel()` from the handler are the primitives. HTTP endpoint is BYO.
`options.signal: AbortSignal` propagates into model and tool calls. Pattern: attach `request.signal` to `options.signal`. No DELETE/cancel endpoint.
`StreamedRunResult.cancel()` interrupts streaming. HTTP-side cancellation works via Starlette closing the connection. No explicit DELETE endpoint.
In-process cancel by dropping the Stream or via `AbortHandle`/`Abortable` from `streaming.rs`. No HTTP cancel endpoint.
`Agent.cancel()` flips a `threading.Event` checked at safe points (during model streaming, before tool execution); returns `stop_reason='cancelled'`. HTTP endpoint exposure is BYO.

`agent.cancel()` flips internal AbortController; `InvokeOptions.cancelSignal: AbortSignal` composes external signals (bind to `req.signal`); cooperative cancellation inside tools via `context.agent.cancelSignal.aborted`. Endpoint is BYO.

Same-server: `chat.stop()` aborts local fetch, mapping to `request.signal` which propagates to `streamText({ abortSignal })`. Multi-server: documented pattern `DELETE /api/chat/:id/stream` writes `canceledAt` to DB; running POST polls via throttled `onChunk` and aborts. Recipe shown in next.js example.

Forwards Gemini's `Partial == true` events on `FunctionCall.Args` as the same `models.Event` frame with `partial:true` and the in-progress args map. Downstream frames complete the args. No dedicated `tool-input-start/delta/end` event taxonomy.

`ToolCallStartedEvent` carries the complete tool call at the moment it is parsed; partial-JSON streaming depends on the model adapter (OpenAI/Anthropic provider-side feature). Agno surfaces the final `tool_args` on `ToolCallStarted`.
`StreamChunk::ToolUseInputDelta { index, partial_json }` emitted in-process while LLM streams tool args. Provider-dependent (Anthropic, OpenAI tool-streaming). Wire framing BYO.
`StreamEvent` carries raw Anthropic SSE events including `input_json_delta`, enabling progressive `Bash command: ls -l /var/` style UIs. Bug-fixed in 0.1.48 for env-var wiring.
Emits `SDKPartialAssistantMessage` wrapping raw `BetaRawMessageStreamEvent` (sdk.d.ts:3226). `input_json_delta` events progressively reveal tool input JSON character-by-character.

`LLMStreamChunkEvent` carries `tool_call: ToolCall | None` with `function.arguments: str` accumulated incrementally. `StreamChunk(chunk_type=TOOL_CALL, tool_call=ToolCallChunk(arguments=...))`. AMP webhook `llm_stream_chunk` carries the same shape.

Tool-call deltas come through streamed `*schema.Message` chunks with `ToolCalls.Index` for merging via `schema.ConcatMessages`. No separate `tool-arg-fragment` event type; you extract from message chunks yourself.

`ToolRequest.Partial bool` flag flows through `ModelResponseChunk` for providers that stream tool args (Gemini supported). No dedicated tool-input-start/delta/end sub-event taxonomy. Plugin-level support varies.
`AIMessageChunk` events on `stream_mode='messages'` carry `tool_call_chunks` field with progressive tool args; final validated args appear on assembled `AIMessage.tool_calls[*].args`.
The LLM's streamed delta of a tool call surfaces via `AgentStream.tool_calls` as the model emits it. Granularity depends on underlying LLM integration.

Three chunk types: `tool-call-input-streaming-start { toolCallId, toolName }`, `tool-call-delta { toolCallId, argsTextDelta }`, `tool-call-input-streaming-end { toolCallId }`. UI can render partial args in real time.
DevUI streams `response.function_call_arguments.delta` (OpenAI Responses convention). AG-UI behaves the same.
OpenAI Responses API emits `response.function_call_arguments.delta` events; they flow through `RawResponsesStreamEvent` directly. End-to-end example at `examples/basic/stream_function_call_args.py`.

Raw model events surface as `RunRawModelStreamEvent` with underlying provider event under `event.data.event` — partial tool args visible if provider streams them. SDK does not normalize into a typed `tool-call-delta` event.
`ToolCallPartDelta` emits incremental `args_delta` strings/dicts via `PartDeltaEvent`. UI adapters (Vercel AI / AG-UI) surface them in their respective dialects.
`StreamedAssistantContent::ToolCallDelta { id, internal_call_id, content }` where content is `Name(String)` or `Delta(String)`. Wire serialization BYO.
`ToolUseStreamEvent` yields `{type: 'tool_use_stream', delta: {...}, current_tool_use: {toolUseId, name, input}}` as the model builds tool arguments. Wire framing is BYO.

Model providers yield `ModelContentBlockDeltaEvent` with `delta: { type: 'toolUseInputDelta', input: '<partial json>' }`. Wrapped as `ModelStreamUpdateEvent`; full `ToolUseBlock` yielded later as `ContentBlockEvent`.

Canonical wire chunks `tool-input-start`, `tool-input-delta` (with `inputTextDelta`), `tool-input-available`. Client `useChat` automatically updates `ToolUIPart.state` from `input-streaming` to `input-available`.

Tool calls `ctx.RequestConfirmation(hint, payload)`; framework emits a `FunctionCall` with name `adk_request_confirmation`. Client decodes, asks user, replies via `/run_sse` with a `functionResponse` matching the original call id. Runner re-runs the tool with the verdict. No separate `/approve` endpoint and no observable pause status (client infers from `LongRunningToolIDs`).

`@tool(requires_confirmation=True | requires_user_input=True | external_execution=True)` pauses the loop and emits `RunPausedEvent` with `status=RunStatus.paused`. Client inspects `run_response.active_requirements`, sends `requirement.confirm/reject`, then `POST /agents/{aid}/runs/{rid}/continue` resumes. Also admin-approvals track under `/approvals/...`.
`AgentHooks::on_tool_call` returning `HookOutcome::Abort` skips the call but there is no pause-and-wait-for-external-approval state — the run cannot be persisted and resumed.

Intra-process: `can_use_tool` callback resolves via `control_response`; for cross-request HITL the client must stay alive in process. `PreToolUse` hook can return `permissionDecision: 'defer'` so `ResultMessage.deferred_tool_use` lets a different process inspect what was deferred.

`canUseTool` is the HITL primitive: SDK awaits a Promise from your callback (correlated by `toolUseID`); for client-visible pause your handler emits a custom SSE frame and resolves the inner Promise on `/approve`. No separate pause-state observable to the client.

Best-in-class design at the Flow layer: `@human_feedback` with `HumanFeedbackProvider`; custom async providers raise `HumanFeedbackPending` which auto-persists state and returns the pending status. External system later calls `flow.resume(feedback=...)`. Tool-level `request_human_input` is console-only. AMP ships a Flow HITL Management UI.

Tools call `adk.Interrupt(ctx, info)` or `adk.StatefulInterrupt`; runner saves checkpoint and emits `InterruptedAgentEvent`. Caller resumes via `runner.ResumeWithParams(ctx, checkpointID, &ResumeParams{Targets: ...})`. No shipped HITL HTTP route.

Two-call protocol: first call yields a model response with `metadata.interrupt` and `finishReason='interrupted'`; second call resumes via `transferTool.RespondWith(part, ...)` or `RestartWith(part, WithResumedMetadata(...))`. Client must persist response/history.

`POST /threads/{tid}/runs/stream` with `command: {resume: 'approved' | {interrupt_id: value}}` is first-class. `StateSnapshot.interrupts` is the observable pause state. State edits via `POST /threads/{tid}/state` compose cleanly with resume.

`ctx.wait_for_event(HumanResponseEvent, waiter_id=..., waiter_event=InputRequiredEvent(...), requirements={...})` pauses inside a tool. Client sees `InputRequiredEvent` on the stream and replies via `handler.ctx.send_event(HumanResponseEvent(...))`. Cleanly typed.

`POST /agents/:id/approve-tool-call` and `decline-tool-call` (plus `-generate` variants for non-streaming) take `{runId, toolCallId}` and return a new SSE stream that resumes execution. `/resume-stream` handles generic tool.suspend; `/observe-stream` lets observers attach mid-stream.

Tools with `approval_mode='always_require'` emit `function_approval_request`; client inspects `result.user_input_requests`, builds `function_approval_response(approved=True|False)`, re-invokes `agent.run(approval_response, session=session)`. DevUI exposes `response.function_approval.requested/responded` events.

Tools mark `function_tool(needs_approval=True | callable)`; `result.interruptions` yields `ToolApprovalItem`s; serialize `RunResult.to_state().to_json()`, on approval `state.approve(interruption)` and re-run. MCP tools have `require_approval='always'|'never'|dict|callable`.

Tools with `needsApproval: true` return `result.interruptions: RunToolApprovalItem[]`. Serialize `result.state`, present approvals, then `state.approve(interruption)` / `state.reject(interruption)` and re-run. End-to-end example shipped.

`@agent.tool(requires_approval=True)` or `raise ApprovalRequired` yields `DeferredToolRequests`. Client gathers approvals, runs again with `deferred_tool_results=DeferredToolResults(approvals={call_id: True}, calls={call_id: ...})`. `HandleDeferredToolCalls` capability allows inline resolution. Explicitly typed primitives.
`PauseControl` only gates polling; no tool-approval-verdict channel. For HITL you implement `on_tool_call -> Skip { reason }` to reject and ask user to re-submit. Cannot persist and resume.

`BeforeToolCallEvent` is `_Interruptible`; a hook raises `InterruptException(Interrupt(name=..., reason=...))` and the agent yields `EventLoopStopEvent` with `stop_reason='interrupt'`. Client re-invokes `agent('...')` with `list[InterruptResponseContent]`. State persisted via session manager.

`context.interrupt({name, reason})` from a tool stores `pendingToolExecution` state and emits `InterruptEvent`s; client resumes with `agent.invoke([{type: 'interruptResponseContent', toolUseId, name, response}])`. New `interventions` subsystem ships structured `Confirm` actions wrapping the interrupt machinery.

Server emits `tool-approval-request` chunk for tools that returned `'user-approval'`. Client `chat.addToolApprovalResponse({id, approved, reason})` then re-POSTs the messages (auto-trigger via `sendAutomaticallyWhen`). No dedicated `/approve` endpoint — same `POST /api/chat` carries everything. Correlated by `approvalId`.
